Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1b) clearly demonstrates a large mass located in the posterior mediastinum, evidenced by its position overlying the lower thoracic spine and forming obtuse angles with the posterior chest wall. This posterior location and smooth contour are characteristic of neurogenic tumors or other posterior mediastinal masses like liposarcoma, distinguishing it from anterior mediastinal pathologies.
